statement.p: A fence is to be built to enclose a rectangular area of 240 square feet. The fence along three sides is to be made of material that costs 4 dollars per foot, and the material for the fourth side costs 15 dollars per foot. Find the dimensions of the enclosure that is most economical to construct.

solution.p: A rectangle has sides x and y. Since the names of the variables don't matter, say one of the y sides costs 15 dollars per foot and the other one and the two sides of length x all cost 4 dollars per square foot. Then the total cost of the fencing is C=4 x + 4 x + 4 y + 15 y= 8 x + 19 y We are trying to minimize this function, but we need to reduce it to one variable. However, we are also given that the area of this rectangle is 240. Thus, xy=240, and solving for one of the variables, y=\frac{240}{x}.

Substituting back into the cost function, we get C= 8 x+ 19 \left(\frac{240}{x} \right) = 8 x+ 4560 x^{-1} Take the derivative and set it equal to 0. C'=8 - 4560 x^{-2}= 8 + \frac{-4560}{x^2}=0 Multiply both sides by x^2 8 x^2-4560=0 and solve x=\sqrt{\frac{4560}{8}}=23.8746727726266 \mbox{ ft.} (Why didn't I know that it wasn't x=-\sqrt{\frac{4560}{8}}=-23.8746727726266 ? )
